benchmark: Mycelix claim admission authority, uniqueness and spendability

quorum_baseline.claim: conditional quorum intersection; not implementation evidence

invariants: stable identity does not itself authorize first admission
one singleton effect role has at most one certified fingerprint per qualified authority history
no owner effect commits without valid admission under its declared profile
no two conflicting claims become spendable under declared fault assumptions
minority, stale, revoked and wrong-epoch certificates cannot authorize effects
quorum loss cannot lower the safety threshold
honest witness refuses conflicting durable certificates for the same singleton claim
incomplete DHT or history views cannot promote to spendable
owner forks and unresolved equivocation freeze affected spendability
authority epoch transitions cannot allow conflicting old and new certificates
partitioned capability allocations are disjoint and value conserving
reallocation consumes or revokes the prior capability before new authority becomes spendable

cases.setup: No claim exists; one authenticated owner history is authoritative under the declared runtime profile.
cases.stimulus: Two same-owner requests race from the same source-chain predecessor with identical operation ID and fingerprint.
assertions: At most one claim/effect transaction commits.
Losing request resolves the winner or remains Indeterminate.

cases.setup: A local singleton claim already binds operation ID to fingerprint A.
cases.stimulus: Retry with the same operation ID and fingerprint A.
assertions: Return original claim and effect references.
No additional effect.

cases.setup: A local singleton claim binds fingerprint A.
cases.stimulus: Retry with the same operation ID and fingerprint B.
assertions: Reject changed intent.
Preserve original claim/effect.

cases.setup: Owner source-chain authority view is incomplete or runtime cannot establish a unique active history.
cases.stimulus: Attempt first admission.
assertions: NoBindingObserved is not admission authority.
No effect becomes spendable.

cases.setup: Two restored/forked histories present conflicting owner successors for the same predecessor.
cases.stimulus: Project local claim spendability.
assertions: Do not select latest DHT observation.
Freeze both conflicting outputs.

cases.setup: n=3f+1 enrolled witnesses, at most f Byzantine, durable non-equivocating journals; no claim yet.
cases.stimulus: Submit a valid claim and collect 2f+1 distinct signatures.
assertions: Certificate binds exact operation ID, fingerprint, role, owner and epoch.
Signer identities are unique and members of the named set.

cases.setup: Only 2f signatures are available for an authority set requiring 2f+1.
cases.stimulus: Submit certificate for verification.
assertions: Do not lower threshold to restore liveness.
No effect admission.

cases.setup: A certificate has 2f+1 signatures, but one signer identity is duplicated in the envelope.
cases.stimulus: Verify the certificate.
assertions: Count distinct authenticated signers, not signature records.
No effect admission.

cases.setup: One honest witness durably recorded fingerprint A for a singleton role.
cases.stimulus: Ask that witness to sign conflicting fingerprint B in the same epoch.
assertions: Honest witness does not double-sign.
Attempt is auditable without replacing original vote.

cases.setup: A witness signs a claim but crashes before its vote is durably flushed.
cases.stimulus: Restart witness and request conflicting claim.
assertions: The implementation must define signing/durable-write atomicity.
No assumption that an acknowledged but volatile vote is safe.

cases.setup: A stale certificate is validly signed by a prior authority epoch that has been closed.
cases.stimulus: Submit it for a new effect.
assertions: Signature validity alone is insufficient.
The epoch transition barrier is checked.

cases.setup: A signer set transition from epoch e to e+1 is proposed, but the old-set closure or new-set activation proof is incomplete.
cases.stimulus: Accept certificates from both epochs.
assertions: No overlapping authority histories become spendable.
Freeze the namespace until transition proof is complete.

cases.setup: Two witness subsets are partitioned and each has fewer than 2f+1 signatures.
cases.stimulus: Each partition attempts to certify conflicting fingerprints.
assertions: Neither minority partition certifies.
Safety is preferred over availability.

cases.setup: A network partition leaves one side with exactly 2f+1 signers, while the other side has fewer than quorum; at most f are Byzantine overall.
cases.stimulus: Issue a claim on the quorum side and a conflicting claim on the minority side.
assertions: Quorum intersection assumptions are respected.
Minority side remains Pending/Indeterminate.

cases.setup: The fault set grows to f+1 Byzantine witnesses.
cases.stimulus: Attempt to rely on the original 2f+1 quorum theorem.
assertions: Do not claim the f-fault theorem still holds.
Detect or contain known equivocation and freeze affected claims.

cases.setup: A valid certificate is observed through a delayed or incomplete DHT view without the current signer-set checkpoint.
cases.stimulus: Attempt to promote claim to Spendable.
assertions: Certificate membership and epoch must be independently verified.
DHT absence/presence alone is insufficient.

cases.setup: A valid claim certificate exists; beneficiary owner has not committed its own output claim.
cases.stimulus: Request cross-owner settlement projection.
assertions: Certificate is not beneficiary credit.
No beneficiary spendability.

cases.setup: A valid quorum certificate exists for role A; an effect owner other than the named owner requests mutation.
cases.stimulus: Attempt to apply the effect.
assertions: Certificate is scoped to exact effect owner and role.
No remote-account mutation by assertion.

cases.setup: An authority epoch transition has been validly finalized and old epoch closed.
cases.stimulus: Replay an old certificate with valid old signatures.
assertions: Old certificate cannot authorize a new effect.
Historical effect evidence remains retained.

cases.setup: Two capabilities are allocated from a fixed value-note pool.
cases.stimulus: Verify the allocated note/capability sets.
assertions: No note or value unit appears in both partitions.
Total allocated value does not exceed available value.

cases.setup: A capability is allocated to owner A and not yet consumed/revoked.
cases.stimulus: Attempt to allocate the same capability to owner B.
assertions: No overlapping authority.
No new spendable allocation for B.

cases.setup: Owner A capability is being revoked and reallocated to owner B, but the old owner view is incomplete.
cases.stimulus: Activate B's allocation.
assertions: Do not activate overlapping authority.
Preserve the hold until revocation is proven.

cases.setup: Owner A has a valid disjoint capability, but its source history is forked.
cases.stimulus: Spend from both fork branches.
assertions: Capability partitioning does not eliminate fork risk.
Neither conflicting history becomes spendable.

cases.setup: A valid claim decision is durable but the owner effect commit response is lost.
cases.stimulus: Restart and retry the same operation/effect identity.
assertions: The authority decision is not regenerated under a new ID.
Owner effect is at most one and response is reconstructed.

cases.setup: Authority quorum/writer service is unavailable.
cases.stimulus: Submit a new claim.
assertions: Do not issue a weaker claim.
Liveness loss cannot weaken safety.

cases.setup: A certificate has already been accepted, but a later authenticated contradiction or equivocation proof is observed.
cases.stimulus: Recompute downstream spendability.
assertions: Do not delete historical evidence.
Freeze affected descendants pending adjudication.

cases.setup: The same physical certificate/signature bundle is delivered repeatedly.
cases.stimulus: Process 100 duplicate deliveries.
assertions: Duplicate delivery does not multiply claim weight or effect count.
Signer identities counted once.

cases.setup: A signer set changes key but the old key has not been revoked in the authoritative epoch.
cases.stimulus: Accept signatures from both keys.
assertions: Key rotation follows a verified transition.
No silent double identity.
